items.title: Contributing quests needed for data related to wheelchair routing
items.body:
Hi,

For a university project, I'm looking for ways to improve OSM coverage regarding data that is needed for wheelchair routing algorithms such as the one used by [Openrouteservice](https://openrouteservice.org/). Given that the solution should be easy to use and does not require users to have previous OSM knowledge, I think that StreetComplete would be a great place to include such crowdsourcing tasks.

As of now, StreetComplete already has some quests that are relevant for wheelchair routing such as the surface type quests. On top of that, I would like to implement quests for the following things:

* Information about **curb types** on pedestrian crossings (see also #1305)
* **Incline** of ways that are relevant for wheelchair routing (using the smartphone's gyroscope to measure exact values)
* **Width** of sidewalks and other paths that are relevant for wheelchair routing (using Google's ARCore SDK for measuring as recently also suggested in #698)
* **Smoothness** of sidewalks and other paths that are relevant for wheelchair routing (see also #1630)
* Potential **barriers** on sidewalks and other paths that are relevant for wheelchair routing

While all of the involved OSM tags are already well-established, they are not used very often, yet. Hence, there may be a large amount of quests that will be generated until the coverage (hopefully) improves over time. Obviously, there are still other difficulties related to each of the proposed quest types, but I don't think that it makes sense to discuss them in great detail using this general issue.

I mainly opened this thread because I'm interested to know if you have some general feedback regarding the idea and to let you know that I would like to work on these things if you are willing to include such accessibility related quest types in StreetComplete (given proper testing etc.). If this is the case, I will create some more detailed quest proposals according to the contribution guidelines over the next couple of weeks (or continue the discussion on already existing ones).

items.title: Quest to determine wheelchair access
items.body:
This pull request addresses #26 implements a quest to ask about the wheelchair accessibility of an object.  There are three possible answers: 'Yes', 'Partial' or 'No'.  These map to wheelchair=yes, wheelchair=limited and wheelchair=no.  I used the word 'Partial' over 'Limited' as I felt it described what was meant more clearly.

The quest is applicable to the following objects:
- all shops except shop=vacant or shop=no
- restaurants
- cafes
- ice cream parlours
- fast food joints
- bars
- pubs
- biergartens
- food courts 
- cinemas

items.title: [quest enhancement] wheelchair:description(:language) as answer to the wheelchair quests
items.body:
### General
Affected tag(s) to be modified/added: [wheelchair:description](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:wheelchair:description) and the language subkeys `wheelchair:description:en`, ... allow for details beyond `wheelchair=yes/no/limited`. Examples are in [wiki Disabilitydescription](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Disabilitydescription#Wheelchair_users_and_other_walking_disabilities). The wheelchair quests could be enhanced to add (or modify, if already present) a description in the local language or a user-chosen language.

The blind and deaf quests could in principle be enhanced the same way, with `blind:description:en` and `deaf:description:en`, but these have very small numbers in taginfo.

<!-- If the answer is not obvious, please add a short explanation below each item. -->
### Checklist
Checklist for quest suggestions (see [guidelines](https://github.com/streetcomplete/StreetComplete/wiki/Adding-new-Quests-to-StreetComplete)):
- [X] 🚧 To be added tag is established and has a useful purpose
- [X] 🤔 Any answer the user can give must have an equivalent tagging (Quest should not reappear to other users when solved by one)
- [X] 🐿️ Easily answerable by everyone from the outside but a survey is necessary
- [X] 💤 Not an overwhelming percentage of quests have the same answer (No spam)
- [X] 🕓 Applies to a reasonable number of map data (Worth the effort)

<!--
All of the above should be fulfilled. 
If you are not sure about how one condition applies to your suggestion or you have (very) strong reasons that a condition may not needed to be satisfied in your case, just note that down. Someone else may come up with some ideas.
-->

### Ideas for implementation

<!-- If you have any idea whether metadata per country is needed, add it here. If you know where to get this data from, mention it here too -->
**Metadata needed:** 

<!-- If you have any idea on how the UI (the form appearing when the quest is asked) should look like.
You can use any way to propose a UI. Feel free to include a mockup. 
Do include all answer possibilities you consider for that quest. -->
**Proposed UI:** Add a button next to the current answers, labeled `Add description` or `Edit descriptions`, depending on the presence of `wheelchair:description` and its language subkeys. The menu `Other answers` would not be appropriate, because the description is complementary (not alternative) to the tristate answers.

### Turnstiles / kissing gates

* note/4508933 - node/281808735 - Gate - Turnstile (node deleted)
* note/4599026 - node/4551927663 - Gate - Turnstile
* note/4657283 - node/5890564551 - Gate - Kissing gate

* note/5479385 - node/6474611662 - Tor - Turnstile

(node deleted) => Node has been removed since the Note was created
Underline => Node has `wheelchair=no` tagged

Currently, `wheelchair=no` is not an exclusion in `nodeFilter` of `AddBarrierOpening`.
Out of [6.7m `barrier=gate` Nodes](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/tags/barrier=gate), [20.8k combine with `wheelchair=no`](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/tags/barrier=gate#combinations).

## Proposed Solution

* Add `and wheelchair != no` to `nodeFilter` of this quest to prevent gates from being tagged this way to appear as an accessibility-quest.
* Allow answering "not suitable for wheelchair users" (or words to that end), which then adds `wheelchair=no` - probably with a "are you sure?" message that re-iterates what the wiki says, you only tag that if you're absolutely sure.

I'm happy to code the solution myself, but I'd like to know y'alls take on this. I am aware that the Wiki does not state `wheelchair=*` as a useful combination with `barrier=gate`, but then again, I wonder if that needs an explicit mention.

items.title: Request to swap 'Partially' and 'Yes' buttons in wheelchair accessibility quests
items.body:
I'd like to propose a small change, that the answers for "Is this place wheelchair accessible?" be reordered to be 
`  Uh... | No | Partially | Yes  `
As it is right now, "Partially" is last. Other quests that have No and Yes options always have Yes on the right, so that position is ingrained as the Yes spot (for me at least). In my mind, "Partially" is somewhere in between No and Yes in meaning, so I feel like it should be in between physically as well.

items.title: Add "not for wheelchairs" answer to AddBarrierOpening quest
items.body:
Resolves #7127.
* Adds "Not suitable for wheelchair access" as a separate answer, that will tag `wheelchair=no`. 
* Changes getApplicableElements to
  * exclude nodes tagged `wheelchair=no` already
  * exclude nodes that are on `highway=stairs` tag are not also tagged with `ramp:wheelchair=yes` or `separate`.
* Adds "otherAnswers" to WidthForm with default empty list so that other width quests don't break.

Test (without automatic uploads) with [this node](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/3752084499).
1. answer handrail, surface, visually impared guides and step count. 
2. Answer the ramp quest with `ramp=no`, download tasks => barrier quest does not show.
3. Undo ramp quest
4. Answer the ramp quest with `ramp:wheelchair=yes`, download tasks => barrier quest DOES show. 
5. Answer Uh ... => not suitable for wheelchair users => Quest icon disappears as expected.

items.title: Ask if restaurants have a wheelchair accessible toilet where `toilets` is not already mapped
items.body:
**Use case**
<!-- Provide a clear and concise description of *your use case* and what you thus think is missing, and why. -->
Wheelchair accessibility of toilets is important information(`toilets:wheelchair`). The quest `AddWheelchairAccessToiletsPart` collects this for anywhere with
```
toilets = yes
and name
and access !~ no|private
```
(and resurvey)

In some countries, essentially all restaurants have toilets and many are not marked with `toilets=yes` so this quest would not show.
(See #1272 and #4860 for reasons for not asking for toilets for all restaurants).

**Proposed Solution**
Extend the element selection to include `amenity~restaurant|pub|bar` or `amenity~cafe|fast_food and indoor_seating=yes` without `toilets=no`. Also, add an other answer "There is no toilet here" to add `toilets=no`
Options:
1) Only apply that extra bit only in countries known to require toilets in restaurants (research to be done).
2) Apply that everywhere, since `AddWheelchairAccessToiletsPart` is disabled by default anyway.

items.title: Do not ask for tactile_paving, wheelchair etc for public_transport=stop_area
items.body:
Not sure if it's actually a bug,

But there exists some misstagging consisting of `railway=station` + `public_transport=stop_area` + `type=public_transport` (mostly likely because of deprecation of `railway=facility` which has sometimes been mistakenly been replaced by `railway=station`).

Seems like SC only looks at `railway=station` (?) for asking things like tactilve_paving, wheelchair etc.
I think it would be sensible to not ask these (and possible similar questions?) for relations which are clearly only grouping all elements of a station together, because wheelchair and tactilve_paving are basically meaningless on these relations or may even be contradictory to actual tags on platforms etc. Probably it also confuses users if they are asked even more often. This would make things more robust.

Example changeset where this happened: [187596748](https://www.openstreetmap.org/changeset/187596748)
(Have already fixed this case now)

items.title: better guidance for wheelchair access quests
items.body:
When I type the info symbol on wheelchair quests I get an explanation that I as a person that knows a few things on that subject find lacking and also does not meet the [description of the wheelchair key in OSM the Wiki](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:wheelchair).

The issue is I kind of really want this quest to keep existing, but I am not at all sure if it is easy, or even atomic ...

Wheelchair access has multiple components, not all of which are even mentioned in the official OSM wiki:
1. is the door wide enough?
2. are there steps?
3. is there accessible seating? (this can also mean is it possible do drive under a table)
4. if there is a counter, is it low enough?
5. Are the paths inside the store wide enough?
6. Are there steps inside?

Some suggestions I would like to add to maybe salvage the quest:

- disable it by default and prompt the user to first read the description of the tag in the official wiki?
- I know it is probably not really an option to split this up into multiple quests, but that would make it atomic
- include a streetmeasure button so I can at least check the width of entrances

items.body:
Added a few more `office` options to the Opening Hours and Wheelchair quests. Also added some that seemed appropriate to the `isShopExpressionFilter` function too.

The following were added because they had more than [10K instances from taginfo](https://taginfo.openstreetmap.org/keys/?key=office#values), and had decent current usage of opening_hours:

- estate_agent (was already in wheelchair and shop expression)
- lawyer (was already in wheelchair)
- telecommunication
- educational_institution
- association
- ngo
- it
- accountant

I only included telecommunication, it, lawyer and accountant in the shop expression, as the others seemed less likely to be present in usual retail environments.

There was no need to change the PlaceName quests as all offices are already included.
